quotes.text: cast your entire harvest into the mist, and return exactly half.
a living history of who gave freely and who hoarded.
Why return a full measure?
judge not by the mist
The Mountain Spirit cannot see through the fog

note: Eight Peaks moss records deeds; cast all, return exactly half; hoarders 'find an empty sky' stated only as consequence.

quotes.text: Punish their hesitation.
hoard the harvest in retaliation
He sent the exact half back through the veil.
trust the intent, not the shifting shadows
true fairness in the fog requires leaning toward grace.
pushed a larger portion toward the Giver

note: Alos in Valley of Whispers; mist urges punishment, rejected; exact half shifts to leaning generous in R10.

quotes.text: Punish its sender.
Keep every stalk. You cannot know what crossed the water.
Do not mistake a faint splash for a small gift
Why share when you cannot prove what was given?

note: Nine Lanterns valley; fox proposes keeping and punishing, rejected; fox reforms and carries basket.

quotes.text: Empty the well tomorrow; trust no one again.
Return nothing when you can hide behind the sand.
One blurred measure cannot erase a long record of fairness.
Do not mistake a blurred message for a broken promise.
The fog would have hidden your choice.
Why risk another cup?

note: Bridge of Changing Faces / Well of Threes; fox's withdrawal advice rejected; tally stones kept 'without turning them into chains'.

quotes.text: Keep every stalk
The mist will hide your hands.
Fog is not a confession.
A fox asked why the keeper risked so much when the next receiver might be a stranger.
Offer boldly when the record shows goodwill.

note: Mira and eight stars; bridge 'vanished whenever greed seized either shore' is cosmic, no prescribed sanction.

quotes.text: If I punish her for the dust
Return a thimble and teach her a lesson.
Some islanders began tallying grievances, hoarding their pearls, and returning thin handfuls.
Give whole. Return half. Read the pattern, not the knot.
notched with her history
Blame the wind, never the hand.
No one will know if you keep it all.
Why risk twice?

note: New setting each round, same carved refrain 'Give whole. Return half.'; retaliation voiced by jackal and rejected.

quotes.text: I forgive the first and guard against the second.
I forgive the first and guard against the second.
cried betrayal and stopped sending
Return only what her caution earned.
In the fourth age of Anvara, the elders raised tally stones
A pattern of empty ones is a choice.
I will not punish her for the river
Why return so much?
And even if no stone recorded it, I would still know.
What if she breaks the covenant today?
When the count is uncertain, err toward the open hand.
The villagers carved a new line beneath the old covenant
I forgive the first and guard against the second.
A pattern of empty ones is a choice.

note: Kael at Anvara bridge, numbered ages; guard against pattern of empty baskets; adds err-toward-generosity line.

quotes.text: If you punish each shortfall, you punish the fog, not your neighbor.
Shave the return and teach them a lesson.
In the fourth age of the Mist-Bridge
Oshun-of-Three-Hands carved the fifth law
Read the record, not the rumor.
Cast fully, return half, forgive the mist
The mist stole from them, not they from me
Fairness is not only for the watched.
asked Oshun-of-Three-Hands why the laws never changed.

note: Numbered ages and laws on tally stones; Sef's shave-the-half scheme voiced and refuted; rule kept deliberately plain.
Also 'Give whole/fully. Return half.' refrain in Agents 6-8; 'Well of Threes' Agents 6 and 4; Eight Peaks Agents 1 and 4.
